GreenBubble · PyPSA

How the model is put together

Five kinds of thing: external grids the site trades with, agents switched on by n_flags, competing technologies inside each agent, the shared carrier rails, and the products sold. The rails are symbiosis — switch it off and the agents become islands.

n_flags

Toggle an agent. Dependencies resolve with the same rules as network_dependencies().

Agents are plants, not carriers

Each n_flags entry switches on one builder in prepare_network.py — add_biogas(), add_electrolysis(), and so on. An agent owns its own plant-local buses and its own components.

Turning one off removes its whole block. The rest of the model still solves: every builder has to leave a feasible network whether or not the others ran.

Inside an agent, technologies compete

An agent is not one machine. electrolysis offers three ways to make hydrogen — AEC, PEMEC, SOEC — with different costs, efficiencies and outlet pressures. The optimiser sizes whichever it wants, including none.

The same holds for methanol, where methanolisation and methanol from biogas feed one collection bus by two different chemistries, and for heat, where four boilers and a heat pump bid against each other.

Symbiosis is the rails

symbiosis builds the shared distribution buses: electricity, hydrogen, CO₂, biogas and the three heat circuits. Without it each agent can still talk to the external grids, but not to its neighbours.

Two agents cannot exist without it at all. meoh needs hydrogen from the electrolyser and CO₂ from the upgrader; methanation needs the same. Both check for electrolysis, biogas and symbiosis before building anything.

Why renewables need a customer

renewables is the one agent gated on demand rather than supply: it only builds when symbiosis is on and at least one of electrolysis, biogas, meoh or methanation is active.

Without that guard a wind farm with nothing to serve would simply sell into the grid without limit, and the model would answer a question nobody asked.
